newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lyttelton Port expects to beat last year's profit.
newsitem.headline: Lyttelton Port expects to beat last year's profit.

text.p: Lyttelton Port said on Tuesday a surge in activity meant it was ahead of budget for the first three months of the year and it now expects to beat last year's profit of NZ$10.5 million.

"The first three months of the new financial year have seen us exceed the assumptions used in our forecasts in the prospectus issued prior to listing on the stock exchange," the company told shareholders at the annual meeting.
"We also expect to exceed last year's annual result.

"We are optimistic that this trend will continue, however, we are mindful that ours is a service industry which depends to a large extent on the success of importers and exporters in a variety of sectors of the economy."
The company said that in many ways it was the South Island's economic barometer, measuring the fortune of New Zealand as a trading nation.

"We are confident in our future but have a weather eye on the economic climate and the potential impact arising from a new MMP government." MMP is the new system of proportional representation which returned a hung parliament in the October 12 general election.
